title: Conormal sequence for a symmetric algebra of a projective quotient conormal module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $A=P/I$, where $I=(f_1,\dots,f_m)$. Put $M=I/I^2$, an $A$-module, and assume $M$ is projective (a direct summand of a free $A$-module). Let $q:A^{\oplus m}\to M$ send the $j$th basis vector to $f_j\bmod I^2$, and let $K=\ker q$. Put $C=\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Let $Q=P[y_1,\dots,y_m]$, let $Q\to C$ extend $P\to A\to C$ and send $y_j$ to the canonical image of $q(e_j)$ in $C$, and put $J=\ker(Q\to C)$. Then $Q\to C$ is surjective, and there is a split exact sequence of $C$-modules $$0\to M\otimes_A C\longrightarrow J/J^2\longrightarrow K\otimes_A C\to0.$$ The first map sends $(f\bmod I^2)\otimes c$ to $c(f\bmod J^2)$, using $I\subseteq J$. The second is induced by reducing $Q\to A[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ modulo $I$ and identifying the conormal module of the resulting presentation of $C$ with $K\otimes_A C$. In particular $J/J^2\cong (M\oplus K)\otimes_A C\cong C^{\oplus m}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CE (lemma-improve-presentation), lines 357-414, especially equation-sequence and its splitting in lines 369-414. The projective case repairs the use of More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07EV: its general claim K tensor C = J/J^2 is false, as recorded in lem-weil-pbc-cotangent-complex-symmetric-algebra. Here q splits, so locally M and K are free, the linear relations corresponding to a basis of K are coordinate variables, and the conormal sequence is exact on the left. Algebra Lemma Tag 00S2 supplies the right-exact sequence.

proof.text: If $A=0$, then $M=K=C=0$, $J=Q$, and $J/J^2=0$, so the assertion is immediate. Assume henceforth $A\neq0$. The displayed map $q:A^{\oplus m}\to M$ is surjective because the classes of the $f_j$ generate $I/I^2$. Projectivity of $M$ supplies a section $s:M\to A^{\oplus m}$, hence $A^{\oplus m}=s(M)\oplus K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] to $M$ and $K$, refining the two finite principal-open covers to a common cover $D(a_i)$ on which both summands are free. The $a_i$ generate the unit ideal. Since $P\to A=P/I$ is surjective, choose a lift $h_i\in P$ of each $a_i$. For each $i$, an adapted basis of $A_{a_i}^{\oplus m}$ identifies the localized map $q_{a_i}$ with projection $A_{a_i}^{r_i}\oplus A_{a_i}^{m-r_i}\to A_{a_i}^{r_i}$. In particular $K\oplus M\cong A^{\oplus m}$ already before localization.

proof.text: Write $B=A[y_1,\dots,y_m]=Q/IQ$ and let $L=\ker(B\to C)$, so $J/IQ=L$ and $IQ\subseteq J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-coefficient-map-kernel], $Q\to B$ is surjective with kernel $IQ$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cotangent-complex-symmetric-algebra] (clauses (1) and (2)), $B\to C$ is surjective, $L$ is generated by the linear forms $\ell(k)=\sum_jk_jy_j$ for $k=\sum_jk_je_j\in K$, and $\lambda:K\otimes_A C\to L/L^2$, $k\otimes c\mapsto c(\ell(k)\bmod L^2)$, is surjective. Thus $Q\to C$ is surjective. Reduction modulo $I$ gives an exact sequence $IQ/(IQ\cap J^2)\to J/J^2\to L/L^2\to0$: the last map sends $j\bmod J^2$ to the class of $j+IQ$ modulo $L^2$, and $L^2=(J^2+IQ)/IQ$ because $L=J/IQ$; its kernel consists exactly of classes represented by $IQ$, with two such representatives equal precisely when their difference lies in $IQ\cap J^2$.

proof.text: Omit any empty $D(a_i)$ from the cover of step 1. On each remaining $D(a_i)$, [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] identify $C_{a_i}$ with $A_{a_i}[u_1,\dots,u_{r_i}]$. Applying the universal property [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] to the two projections of $A_{a_i}^{m}=M_{a_i}\oplus K_{a_i}$ identifies $B_{a_i}$ with $A_{a_i}[u_1,\dots,u_{r_i},v_1,\dots,v_{m-r_i}]$ so that $B_{a_i}\to C_{a_i}$ sets every $v_l$ to zero. Consequently $L_{a_i}=(v_1,\dots,v_{m-r_i})$; these variables are a regular sequence by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] identifies $L_{a_i}/L_{a_i}^2$ with the free $C_{a_i}$-module on their classes. The map $\lambda_{a_i}$ of step 2 takes the corresponding basis of $K_{a_i}\otimes_{A_{a_i}}C_{a_i}$ to these classes, so it is bijective. Its kernel and cokernel vanish on a principal-open cover; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] makes localization preserve these kernels and cokernels, and the unit-ideal cover forces them to vanish globally. Hence $\lambda:K\otimes_A C\cong L/L^2$.

proof.text: Omit any empty member of the cover from step 1. On each remaining member choose the lift $h_i\in P$ from step 1 and apply [lem-weil-pbc-conormal-intersection-regular-quotient] to $(IQ)_{h_i}\subseteq J_{h_i}$: the quotient $J_{h_i}/(IQ)_{h_i}=L_{a_i}$ is generated by the regular sequence $v_1,\dots,v_{m-r_i}$ from step 3. It gives $(IQ)_{h_i}\cap J_{h_i}^2=((IQ)_{h_i})J_{h_i}$. The quotient of $IQ\cap J^2$ by $IQJ$ is a $C$-module, since multiplication by $J$ sends $IQ$ into $IQJ$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], its localization at every $a_i$ vanishes; since the $a_i$ generate $1$ in $A$ and hence in $C$, it vanishes globally. Thus $IQ\cap J^2=(IQ)J$. Define $\theta:(I/I^2)\otimes_A C\to IQ/IQJ$ by $\theta((f\bmod I^2)\otimes c)=\widetilde c f\bmod IQJ$, for any lift $\widetilde c\in Q$ of $c\in C$. This is well defined: changing $\widetilde c$ by an element of $J$ changes the result by $IQJ$, changing $f$ by $I^2$ changes it by $I^2Q\subseteq IQJ$, and the tensor balancing relation is multiplication by a lift from $A$ (which commutes in $Q$). Conversely, expand an element of $IQ$ coefficientwise as a polynomial with coefficients in $I$ and reduce its coefficients modulo $I^2$ and its monomials modulo $J$; this gives the inverse to $\theta$. Hence $(IQ)/(IQJ)\cong(I/I^2)\otimes_A C=M\otimes_A C$. Together with $IQ\cap J^2=(IQ)J$, the map in the statement $M\otimes_A C\to J/J^2$ is injective, with image the kernel of $J/J^2\to L/L^2$ from step 2.

proof.text: Compose the right map of step 2 with the inverse of $\lambda$ from step 3. Together with the injection and kernel computation of step 4 it gives the stated short exact sequence. The right term $K\otimes_A C$ is projective over $C$: tensor the splitting $A^{\oplus m}=M\oplus K$ with $C$, so $K\otimes_A C$ is a direct summand of $C^{\oplus m}$. Therefore the surjection $J/J^2\to K\otimes_A C$ splits. Choosing a section yields $J/J^2\cong(M\otimes_A C)\oplus(K\otimes_A C)\cong(M\oplus K)\otimes_A C\cong C^{\oplus m}$.
